title: Nike ends Adidas’ Champions League ball reign with €40m-a-year deal
article_text:
Nike will take over as the official match ball provider of the Uefa Champions League from next season, ending its German sportswear rival Adidas’ 25-year association with European soccer’s premier competition.

The deal, which runs until the end of the 2030/31 campaign, will also see Nike replace Decathlon brand Kipsta as the ball supplier of the Europa League and Conference League, marking the first time one company has fulfilled the role for all three Uefa men’s club competitions.

Adidas supplied the Europa League from 2009 to 2018, when it was replaced by Molten, but has never partnered with the third-tier Conference League, which has been bundled with the secondary competition’s commercial agreements since it was launched in 2021. Molten was supplanted by Kipsta in 2024.

Financial terms were not disclosed, but SportsPro understands that the deal is worth around €40 million (US$44 million) per year. The figure was originally reported by the Financial Times, which said the fee doubled the value of the current agreement.

Nike previously supplied the ball for the Champions League final between 1998 and 2001 before losing the contract to Adidas, whose rights were expanded to every match in the competition.

However, Nike looked set to regain the contract when Uefa men’s club competition commercial rights owner UC3 and its global sales agency Relevent Football Partners (RFP) entered exclusive negotiations with the company in April following a competitive tender process launched a month earlier.

Further information around match ball designs are expected in due course. It is unclear whether Nike will be able to incorporate the star pattern that has become synonymous with Adidas’ match balls, with The Guardian reporting that the German company holds rights to the design.

“Football is the world’s game, and the ball is at the centre of it, the one thing every player, in every competition, has in common,” said Camilo Andrade, vice president and general manager of Nike Football.

“This is a long-term commitment for Nike. We will listen to the athlete’s voice, push the edges of innovation, honour the prestige and tradition of these competitions, and make sure the ball represents the instinct, creativity and joy football brings to billions of fans.”

The move will be seen a boost for Nike, whose chief executive Elliott Hill has named soccer as one of the company’s priority sports in his strategy to revive the brand’s fortunes after returning to the business in 2024. The deal was confirmed on the eve of Nike’s investor day on 17th November.

The deal also fills a gap in Nike’s soccer portfolio. The company has been without a major ball supply deal in men’s European soccer since the Premier League switched to Puma, another German company, from the 2025/26 season, ending a 25-year association with Nike.

Nike also recently saw Kylian Mbappe, one of its most high-profile athletes and one of the best players in the world, opt to sign a boot deal with Swiss upstart On rather than extend his relationship with the company.

Even so, Nike retains an extensive presence in soccer, including kit supply deals with several Champions League regulars, such as holders Paris Saint-Germain, Spanish giants FC Barcelona and reigning Italian champions Inter.

The ball supply deal represents the latest category shakeup since RFP replaced Team Marketing, which had sold the rights to Uefa’s men’s club competitions for more than three decades as UC3’s exclusive global sales agency.

RFP has introduced a new tiered sponsorship structure, headlined by four premium partner slots which offer brands the opportunity to strike deals covering all three men’s club competitions. Sponsors can also sign global deals covering specific tournaments.

Although Nike’s deal covers all three competitions, its supplier status means it will not take one of the premier partner slots, nor will it be listed as a global sponsor.

Speaking to SportsPro earlier this year, Charlie Marshall, chief executive of the European Football Clubs body and co-managing director of UC3, said the organisation was “happy to shake things up” while leaving the door open to existing partners.

That has been borne out during the current sales cycle. One of the first major sponsorship deals saw Anheuser-Busch InBev end Heineken’s longstanding grip on the beer category in an agreement reportedly worth €200 million (US$232 million) per year.

Alibaba and existing partner PepsiCo have also signed top-tier deals for the 2027 to 2033 cycle, while Haier and Hyundai will be global sponsors of the Champions League.

It is understood that the sales process has already secured more revenue than the current cycle and is on course to deliver more than €1 billion in annual commercial income for Uefa.

Despite losing the men’s Champions League contract, Adidas remains the official match ball supplier for the women’s tournament and Uefa’s national team competitions, including Euro 2028 and the Nations League.

Al-Mussahal Thanks the Leadership for the Historic Achievement of the Kingdom Winning the Right to Host the 2034 World Cup - Saudi Arabian Football Federation
article_text:
Saudi Football Federation Board Chairman Yasser bin Hassan Al-Mussahal, in his name and on behalf of board members, extended his highest thanks and gratitude to the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud - may God support him - and to His Royal Highness Prince Mohammed bin Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, Crown Prince and Prime Minister - may God protect him - for the generous support of the sports sector, which today bore fruit in the historic achievement of the Kingdom winning the right to host the 2034 World Cup.

The Saudi Federation President appreciated the great support from the Crown Prince, with direct supervision and continued attention, which had the greatest impact on the file receiving the highest evaluation in the history of World Cup bids.

The Saudi Federation President extended sincere thanks to His Royal Highness Prince Abdulaziz bin Turki Al-Faisal, Minister of Sport and President of the Saudi Olympic and Paralympic Committee, for his continued attention and follow-up of the 2034 World Cup hosting bid file, as he devoted all capabilities to presenting an exceptional and historic file.

Al-Mussahal thanked FIFA and the "FIFA Congress" members for the great confidence enjoyed by the Kingdom's 2034 World Cup hosting file, affirming the Kingdom's commitment to delivering a historic edition that brings together fans from around the world on the Kingdom's land, which always welcomes everyone.

The Saudi Football Federation President said on this historic occasion: "Winning the right to host the 2034 World Cup is a dream come true for the nation's sons who have great passion for football, paving the way for an exceptional edition that gives fans from all over the world an unforgettable experience."

Al-Mussahal added: "The Kingdom has made great strides in football over the past years to achieve this dream, which writes a new history so that the Kingdom's journey forward continues under wise leadership that always looks toward a brighter future."

The Saudi Federation President pointed out that over the past few years the Kingdom has gained a great reputation as a leading sports hub worldwide, in light of its successful hosting of more than 100 international sporting events, so that the 2034 World Cup will be a crowning of this leadership, which we promise everyone will continue and develop in a way that contributes to developing world sport and achieves the aspirations of sports fans.

title: Why the WTA is ready to build its own merchandise business
article_text:
The Women’s Tennis Association (WTA) is making its biggest move into the merchandise category in its 53-year history.

At last week’s WTA Finals in Indian Wells, the tour unveiled its first-ever official merchandise collaboration with Japanese entertainment company Sanrio’s Hello Kitty to create co-branded t-shirts, sweatshirts and a collectible plush. That was followed by further partnerships with women’s sports media and commerce company Togethxr and Monarch Commerce, which will launch the tour’s first online fan shop next year.

The push into consumer products comes a year after WTA Ventures, the organisation’s commercial arm, launched a refreshed brand identity for the tour as part of a wider strategy to build a lifestyle brand that has relevance beyond the sport itself.

Established in 2023 to drive new revenue into the sport, WTA Ventures has so far focused on growing the tour’s sponsorship and media rights income. Speaking to SportsPro, WTA chief brand officer Sarah Swanson said merchandise has always been part of the plan.

“We wanted to make sure first we had our brand in order,” she said. “Now, we’re looking at ways that we can take it to market outside of the traditional sponsorship assets and media rights. The consumer products space fell squarely in that plan.”

Given the history and prestige of the WTA, some might wonder why the tour hasn’t made a more concerted push into merchandise until now. More than four million spectators attended its events in 2025 and the organisation boasts nearly three million YouTube subscribers, two million followers on Instagram and 1.4 million on TikTok.

Swanson pointed out that unlike team sports, where supporters routinely show their allegiance through club merchandise, fandom in sports like tennis centres on individual athletes. That has historically left the tour with less room to capitalise on its own branded products.

One of the WTA’s priorities now is to give its longstanding fans a visible way to express their connection to women’s tennis.

“This is the first time where people who have been fans of women’s tennis for a really long time are able to show that fandom,” Swanson said.

She added that merchandise has traditionally been viewed as the bottom of the funnel: fans discover a sport, fall in love with it and eventually purchase products. However, as the WTA looks to reach new audiences, Swanson believes this dynamic can also work in reverse.

“In many cases, the product can be the top of the funnel,” she continued. “You come across a piece of merchandise that you really love and buy it, and then think, let me check out the sport that sits behind this really cool piece of merchandise.

“And I think for us, it’s going to be both ends of that.”

Given the WTA’s pioneering role in women’s sport, it seems apt that it is expanding into merchandise alongside three partners shaped by women. Hello Kitty, which debuted just one year after the WTA was founded in 1973, was created by a female designer, while Togethxr and Monarch are both women-founded businesses.

The partnership with Hello Kitty is being delivered through three of Sanrio’s existing licensees, Wild Collective, Forever Collectibles and Homage. Swanson said WTA Ventures has entered a relationship with each of those companies, which is “something that we’ll build on in the future”.

Hello Kitty is also no stranger to women’s sport, with Sanrio having previously struck partnerships with the likes of the Ladies Professional Golf Association (LPGA), all-female racing series F1 Academy and the International Cricket Council (ICC) for the 2026 Women’s T20 World Cup.

Meanwhile, the Togethxr tie-up is an expansion of an existing relationship which has seen the pair work together editorially. The latest collaboration kicked off with the launch of a women’s tennis-themed collection of the hugely popular ‘Everyone Watches Women’s Sports’ T-shirt.

“We’ve always believed the demand for women’s sports merchandise was there, but the availability, creativity and investment in the product hadn’t caught up with the audience,” Bailey Williamson, senior vice president of partnerships at Togethxr, told SportsPro.

“That’s changing, and partnerships like this are helping accelerate it.

“When you give fans something they’re genuinely excited to wear, you’re creating more than a transaction. You’re building community, driving visibility and giving people another way to show up for women’s sports.”

While Hello Kitty and Togethxr will provide further cultural relevance for the WTA and help take the tour’s brand into new spaces, Monarch Commerce will play more of an operational role, ensuring fans can buy the new products.

A subsidiary of women’s sports private equity firm Monarch Collective, the company already has partnerships with the Women’s National Basketball Association’s (WNBA) Atlanta Dream and Just Women’s Sports.

As Samantha Bushy, chief executive at Monarch Commerce, put it: “We are the feet underneath the swan, designing the product, bringing the product in, setting up the store and running the store. But for consumers, it should just look like a WTA-branded store.”

The online shop is set to launch in spring 2027, with Monarch Commerce adopting a test-and-learn approach that will allow the tour to refine its product offering as it gathers data on what resonates with fans.

The initial product range will be anchored by white-label, WTA-branded merchandise that draws heavily on the tour’s visual identity. Licensed products from Hello Kitty and Togethxr will also be available, making the store a one-stop shop for women’s tennis merch.

“It’s going to be well beyond T-shirts,” said Bushy. “It’s going to be jackets, sweatshirts, hats, visors, bags, shorts.

title: Stop clock, ‘batter zones,’ and lots of Afghan players: What is new about ILT20?
article_text:
The fifth season of the DP World International League T20 starts on Saturday.

Desert Vipers, the defending champions, will face MI Emirates in the opening match at Dubai International Stadium.

It is a rematch of last year’s final, when the side that had won the most matches in the competition’s history finally won the title for the first time.

The 20-over competition involves six teams who play each other twice over the league phase, before play-offs and a final.

Although nominally a league for the UAE, “international” is the operative word.

Unlike the overwhelming majority of leagues elsewhere in the world, ILT20 sides can have as many as nine overseas players in each starting XI.

It is a rule the ICC have sanctioned, but is now reportedly looking into ending.

Desert Vipers, who are owned by US businessman Avram Glazer, are the only side not associated with another franchise from India.

Dubai Capitals are the sister team of the Delhi franchise in the IPL of the same name.

Abu Dhabi Knight Riders are an offshoot of the side originally set up in Kolkata, while MI Emirates originate from the Mumbai franchise in the IPL.

Gulf Giants and Sharjah Warriorz have sister teams in India’s Women’s Premier League.

Each playing XI must now include at least two UAE players, two Afghans and one from an Associate (non-Test playing) country.

The Associate player can also be a UAE player, giving a typical line-up of six international players, two UAE, two Afghanistan and one Associate player.

The same minimum must be on the field at all times while a team is fielding.

It seems odd that sides are obligated to have as many Afghans as UAE players. It is part of a strategy aimed at ensuring Afghans choose the ILT20 if there is a scheduling clash with other leagues at any point in the future.

The rule has been retained where teams can replace a player with a substitute.

It is going to take some administration: when a Super Sub is introduced, the team must still keep at least two UAE, two Afghans and one Associate player in their XI.

If an international player has batted and completed their innings and is then replaced by another international player, the UAE, Afghans and Associates are not required to bat in that innings.

The league is introducing a “batter zone” for deciding wides. The zone runs between the inside edges of the off- and leg-side wide lines at the popping crease.

Umpires will signal a wide if the whole ball passes outside the batter zone at the popping crease, or passes above the head height of the striker standing upright at the crease.

“Even if the batter moves to bring the ball within reach, the umpire will call and signal wide if no part of the ball passes the popping crease inside the zone and the batter does not make contact,” league rules state.

“The only exception is when the batter plays a reverse sweep or switch hit, in which case both off-side wide lines shall apply.

“Umpires have been instructed to apply the law strictly and consistently to stop negative bowling wide of the wicket.”

A 60-second clock between the end of one over and the start of the next – by which time bowlers need to be ready – was already implemented.

Now, though, it also applies to the batting side. Both batters must be ready to start the next over within a minute of the previous over ending. They will get two warnings per innings.

“On the third and any later occasion, the umpire will award five penalty runs to the fielding side,” league rules now state.

“The clock does not apply when a new batter comes to the wicket between overs, during approved injury treatment, strategic time-outs, stoppages for ground, weather or light, third-umpire referrals and reviews, or other delays beyond the batting side’s control, such as broken equipment. Glove changes are not an exemption.”

title: Dana White's UFC fighter loan system faces scrutiny after RAF Abu Dhabi brawl arrests
article_text:
Dana White's UFC fighter loan system faces scrutiny following a series of violent incidents at Real American Freestyle wrestling events.

Merab Dvalishvili was involved in a fight by a group led by Usman Nurmagomedov in Abu Dhabi, resulting in 10 arrests and multiple convictions.

Usman Nurmagomedov's prospective UFC signing and his brother Umar's career prospects have been severely damaged by their six-month prison sentences.

The UFC has a history of tolerating pre-fight confrontations, with incidents involving Conor McGregor and others having become defining moments in the sport.

"It's crazy. I mean, they must like it for this to happen all the time," UFC president Dana White said of the recurring incidents.

Dana White has built a global sporting empire on the backs of fighters who are as adept at selling a fight outside the octagon as they are at winning one inside it.

But the UFC president may be discovering that when his stars step outside the organisation, the theatre of pre-fight promotion can spill over into something altogether more serious.

White has been happy to see some of his biggest names compete on Real American Freestyle (RAF) wrestling cards. But a series of ugly confrontations, culminating in last week's extraordinary scenes in Abu Dhabi, could force him to reconsider.

Initially, letting his MMA fighters compete on RAF wrestling cards made sense. There's no striking involved, so the risk of serious injuries and concussions is greatly reduced. It keeps athletes active in between fights and exposes them to a new audience.

To recap, Merab Dvalishvili, the former UFC bantamweight champion, was ambushed by a group led by fellow MMA fighter Usman Nurmagomedov in the lobby of the Yas Hilton hotel ahead of his appearance at RAF Abu Dhabi.

Police made 10 arrests. The Abu Dhabi Criminal Court subsequently convicted eight of those involved, with Dvalishvili and his accomplice, Saba Lazishvili, fined Dh50,000 each and released.

Footage of the attack went viral. Two of those convicted were jailed after publishing footage of the brawl.

It was bad for everyone involved, not least the Nurmagomedovs. Usman was in talks to sign with the UFC after becoming a free agent following the expiration of his PFL contract. Umar was already on the UFC roster. It is hard to see how either has a future in the organisation.

It followed another high-profile brawl involving two of White's star UFC names at the pre-fight press conference ahead of RAF 14 last month.

On that occasion, Arman Tsarukyan tried to get at Dillon Danis, a rent-a-gob jiu-jitsu practitioner who likes to antagonise his opponents with racial slurs and provocative statements.

Danis wore a T-shirt that depicted Khamzat Chimaev, another stud in the UFC stable who was sat in the front row, in a less than favourable light. A melee ensued before security got control of the situation.

That was spillover from Danis' loss to Chimaev at RAF 10. The UAE combat star pinned Danis in 44 seconds and kicked him up the backside as he lay on the mat after the referee's whistle, resulting in members of both teams storming the stage.

On Sunday, White was asked if the UFC was reconsidering loaning their fighters out to the RAF following a spate of incidents.

"It's crazy. I mean, they must like it for this to happen all the time," White said, shaking his head.

His frustration is understandable. A deal for Usman, the undefeated PFL lightweight champion and a genuine star, looks dead in the water. His brother Umar, a former world title contender at bantamweight, is unlikely to fight again until at least the back end of 2027, if he is retained at all.

Dvalishvili, the former UFC bantamweight champion, was lucky to suffer only cuts and bruises to his face following the attack. That he competed at RAF Abu Dhabi this past Saturday – and then called for Usman and his associates to be immediately released – is a testament to his character.

It's important to acknowledge that the UFC does RAF a favour in loaning out its fighters to compete against genuine world-class wrestlers and Olympians. It elevates RAF, something CEO and co-founder Chad Bronstein acknowledges.

But from White's perspective, the CEO of a multibillion-dollar company doesn't want his fighters involved in violent altercations unless they are in the confines of a UFC octagon.

It also seems a bit rich that a man happy to let flames be fanned to sell a fight in his own organisation objects to it being done in others.

Fighters taking it to each other ahead of fights or at press conferences is nothing new, and certainly not in the UFC.

Conor McGregor specialised in it. Before his first fight with Nate Diaz in 2016, he and his camp exchanged insults and threw water bottles and cans at each other as the event descended into mayhem.

The Irishman and his entourage attacked a bus carrying Khabib Nurmagomedov – the trainer and cousin of Usman and Umar – and other fighters at Barclays Centre in Brooklyn ahead of UFC 299.

The incident left several fighters injured and became one of the defining moments in UFC history. The rivalry culminated in a post-fight brawl after Khabib submitted McGregor at UFC 229.

During a promotional press conference ahead of UFC 178, light-heavyweight rivals Jon Jones and Daniel Cormier went head-to-head before Jones shoved Cormier. Both fighters started swinging, knocking over the promotional backdrop and sending security scrambling.

title: Pro Climbing League raises £3.2m to expand after London sell-out
article_text:
The Pro Climbing League has raised £3.2m in seed funding to take independent professional climbing to more cities, after selling 4,000 tickets for its 2027 season on the first day.

Redrice Ventures led the round. Redrice counts Andy Murray and Alistair Brownlee as associate partners and was an early backer of British sportswear brand Castore. It was joined by Active Partners, London-based sports fund Accelerate Ventures and the International Bouldering Alliance, a European gym group. PCL describes the investment as one of the first times institutional capital has backed a climbing event or media brand outside the gym environment.

The funding will underpin a three-event season in 2027: Berlin on 23rd January 2027, Paris on 13th February 2027 and London on 20th March 2027. Five events are planned for 2028, including one in the US.

PCL’s London debut in February sold out in less than a day, with 2,500 seats available. In the women’s final, France’s Oriane Bertone beat double Olympic champion Janja Garnbret in front of more than 2,400 spectators. Some 43% of ticket buyers were female, and attendees came from 27 countries.

Danaan Markey, CEO of the Pro Climbing League, said, “We sold 4,000 tickets in the first day and are steadily climbing.”

Demand has led PCL to bring its expansion plans forward by a year and move to larger venues. The business earns revenue from tickets and sponsorship, with Red Bull, which broadcast the London event, as a major partner.

Prize money is central to the model. First place at major international events currently pays £6,000, while the London winners each took home £10,000. The prize pot will rise to £50,000 per event in 2027.

PCL was founded by Markey, a former German national team coach and Patagonia sports marketer, alongside climbing commentator Charlie Boscoe, former BBC Radio head of live events Neil Wyatt, and start-up operator Eelco Bulten.

Alistair Brownlee, Associate Partner at Redrice Ventures, said indoor climbing has grown from a subculture into a global phenomenon, pointing to mass participation, Olympic status and growing media recognition. He added that today’s climbers want to compete in and watch their sport, creating an audience with real commercial value.

title: Canadian insurance sponsorships are reshaping carrier brand strategy
article_text:
Canadian insurance sponsorships reached a new level of strategic intent in 2026, and the stakes for brokers are more concrete than they might appear. Carriers that do not distribute through independent brokers are using sports and community partnerships as their primary mechanism for building consumer familiarity – the kind of name recognition that broker relationships provide for other carriers organically. The broker question is not abstract: IBC’s own survey data shows the share of Canadian insurance clients who say they always rely fully on their broker’s recommendation to choose an insurer has fallen from 45% in 2024 to 35% in 2026. When clients arrive at a broker conversation having already formed a view of a carrier, that is partly a function of brand exposure. Sports sponsorship is one of the main ways carriers are creating that exposure.

The numbers frame the gap. According to the Canadian Life and Health Insurance Association’s (CLHIA) 2026 annual factbook, released October 20, 2026, 84% of life insurance in Canada – totalling $6.2 trillion in coverage across 23 million Canadians – is purchased through individual agents and advisors. Carriers that cannot access that channel must build consumer recognition another way. They are spending more doing so: according to the 2026 Canadian Sponsorship Landscape Study, released August 18, 2026, by T1 and the Sponsorship Marketing Council Canada, total sponsorship spending in Canada reached $4.7 billion – with brands planning to increase investment further.

Securian Canada’s activation at the 113th Grey Cup in November 2026 illustrates the approach. The Toronto-based insurer, which distributes creditor, group life, critical illness, and affinity products through banks, credit unions, and affinity groups rather than through independent brokers, has been the official life insurance partner of the Canadian Football League (CFL) since 2023. As part of that partnership, it also presents the CFL’s Diversity in Football programme, which provides career development pathways in professional football coaching and operations. For the 2026 Grey Cup, Securian Canada ran its second Game Changers contest – Kayla McNulty, a physical education teacher at Morin Heights Elementary School in Morin-Heights, Quebec, was selected from 381 nominations for launching her school’s first flag football programme. On November 15, 2026, she joined Securian Canada to present the Most Valuable Player award in Calgary.

“The people who make the greatest difference in our communities don’t always seek recognition. They’re the ones who see potential where others see barriers,” Nigel Branker, chief executive officer of Securian Canada in Toronto, said in the company’s November 12, 2026, press release.

The programme is in its second year. Its inaugural 2025 winner, James Dickens, was recognised for more than 18 years as a firefighter, coaching youth football, and more than 22 years of military service. Securian Canada’s 2025 Beyond Business Report records that Dickens was nominated while navigating treatment for stage-four cancer, attended the Grey Cup in Winnipeg with his partner, and passed away in December 2025.

Securian Canada is not the only carrier using sport as a consumer brand channel. Allstate Canada, which distributes through its exclusive captive agent network, extended its official insurance partnership with Canada Soccer and the Canadian Premier League through 2030, confirmed in June 2026. Like Securian Canada, its sports investment functions primarily as a direct-to-consumer visibility play.

Beneva, Canada’s largest mutual insurer, distributes through brokers and advisors outside Quebec – a commitment it reaffirmed as part of its January 2026 merger with Gore Mutual. It has nonetheless been building a national portfolio of running event title sponsorships since its 2020 formation, with the Calgary Marathon announced in September 2026 becoming its seventh running event in Canada, as IBC’s coverage of Beneva’s growing national running sponsorship strategy across Canadian cities has documented. Intact Insurance, which distributes through both independent brokers via its Intact brand and directly through belairdirect, became the national partner of the Canadian Olympic Committee in October 2025, running through the 2028 Los Angeles Summer Games.

For broker-distributed carriers, sports partnerships serve a different purpose than they do for non-broker carriers. Consumer-facing brand investment can reinforce the value of the broker relationship – a client who arrives already recognising a carrier name requires less education at the point of advice. That is the more benign reading. The less comfortable reading, supported by the decline in full broker reliance noted above, is that carriers building direct consumer familiarity through sport are quietly shifting the dynamics of the advice conversation before a client ever reaches a broker.

Brokerages have increasingly entered the sports sponsorship market in response. Western Financial Group, one of Canada’s largest national insurance brokerages, entered a multi-year CFL jersey sponsorship with the Winnipeg Blue Bombers in February 2026, following a similar deal with the Calgary Stampeders that established its western Canadian brand presence through sport. HUB International signed a multi-year deal as the official employee benefits partner of the Professional Women’s Hockey League (PWHL) in Canada, covering five Canadian markets from the 2026-27 season. Navacord partnered with the Toronto Maple Leafs, and Acera Insurance and Navacord jointly signed a deal with Vancouver Whitecaps FC through the 2027-28 season.

For brokerages, the aim is national brand credibility – differentiating on something other than price or product access in a market where the Insurance Brokers Association of Canada’s Broker Identity Program attracted renewal commitments from more than a dozen carriers in 2026, funding advertising and advocacy on the broker channel’s behalf. For independent brokers, the practical implication is direct: when both non-broker carriers and large consolidator brokerages are investing in consumer recognition through sport, the independent broker’s most defensible position is the advice relationship itself. Brokers and agents held 58% of the Canadian P&C market as of 2025, according to the Custom Market Insights Canada Property & Casualty Insurance Market report. That majority rests on the value of advice – and the sponsorship investments of carriers that do not use brokers are, in effect, a bet that consumer familiarity can begin to substitute for it.

title: What’s left to race for at F1 Las Vegas Grand Prix after champion decided? - Las Vegas Review-Journal
article_text:
The Formula One drivers and constructors world championships have both been decided heading into this week’s Las Vegas Grand Prix.

But there’s still plenty of stakes on the line for a handful of the other 21 drivers.

There will be a little less buzz when F1 returns to The Strip for the Las Vegas Grand Prix after 20-year-old Kimi Antonelli won the drivers’ championship last month after a dominant season and Mercedes clinched the constructors championship on Nov. 8 in Brazil.

All attention will be on the battle for second place where five drivers are separated by 33 points for the runner-up spot behind Antonelli with three races remaining in the season.

Action around the 17-turn, 3.853-mile course around the Strip begins on Thursday night with two practice sessions (4:30 and 8 p.m.). The 50-lap Las Vegas Grand Prix is at 8 p.m. Saturday.

Four-time champion Max Verstappen sits second in the points (279 points), 111 points behind Antonelli. But behind Verstappen sits George Russell (262 points), Lewis Hamilton (261), Charles Leclerc (249) and 2025 champion Lando Norris (246).

All five drivers can get the second spot in the standings, but the path to the runner-up spot will first take navigating the Las Vegas Strip circuit.

“I have no idea because Vegas is so different and so difficult for everyone to understand,” Verstappen said in a postrace news conference after his second-place finish in Brazil on Nov. 8 when asked if he thinks he’ll be the car to beat in Las Vegas.

“It’s a very long straight, so I think I would need to tuck in in the middle of the straight to try and gain some top speed. That is just the game this year with energy management on that straight. It’s going to be very, very difficult.”

Verstappen is the defending winner of the Las Vegas Grand Prix and has won twice at the track. He is riding a streak of eight straight podium finishes (which includes three wins in the stretch) and 11 podiums in the past 13 races.

“It’s so cold over there that you get very different behavior from every car,” Verstappen told reporters in Brazil about the characteristics of the Las Vegas track. “Some suddenly work extremely well on a track like that. We’ve seen it in the past. I have to say that it’s normally not our best track because of that, but we’ll see if we can get the tires to work. That’s the key, to be honest, around there.”

Norris’ title-defense season has not gone according to plan. His win in Brazil earlier this month was his third of the year but sixth total podium finish through 20 races.

Norris, driving for McLaren, finished second in last year’s Las Vegas Grand Prix, but shortly after the race was disqualified due to excessive rearmost skid plank wear. Still, Norris has a chance to finish as the season’s runner-up in a down year for McLaren.

“There’s always pressure every time I put my helmet on because I need to do well, the team require me to do well, and I want to do well for myself,” Norris told reporters in Brazil. “Maybe there’s more pressure from external situations, but any time I go on track, there’s pressure to perform and to do the best job I can.

“I feel the same this year as I felt last year. Especially in these conditions, you always feel a lot of pressure. So, I felt very similar this year to last year, and that’s just normal.”

Norris and his McLaren teammate’s double disqualification in Las Vegas last year moved Antonelli into third place, for the Italian driver’s third podium finish of his 2025 rookie season.

Antonelli was in contention to win in Brazil, but a spin cost him a chance at a 10th win of the season and he finished fifth as Mercedes locked up the constructors title. But Antonelli said after Brazil he is looking forward to getting another chance to contend more wins beginning in Las Vegas.

“I really want to finish on a high and hopefully come back … finish with a couple more wins and finish the season on a high,” Antonelli said to F1.com after his Brazil finish. “All we want is to keep the momentum going, as well into 2027, and the goal is to keep being successful.”

title: Alzheimer’s Research UK becomes World Seniors Snooker charity partner
article_text:
Alzheimer’s Research UK has joined the World Seniors Snooker Tour as its charity partner, bringing the sport’s most recognisable veteran names behind the push for a cure for dementia.

The partnership will raise awareness of dementia and the need for research, while creating opportunities to generate funds for the charity’s work. The Tour will use its events, platforms and profile within the sport to spotlight Alzheimer’s Research UK and encourage players, fans and supporters to back the cause.

Alzheimer’s Research UK is the largest UK charity dedicated to dementia research. It funds research, challenges misconceptions and supports everyone affected by a condition that touches millions of families across the country.

Rohit Sagoo, Director at the World Seniors Snooker Tour, said, “We are absolutely delighted to welcome Alzheimer’s Research UK as our official charity partner. Dementia is a cause that touches so many people and families, and we are proud to be able to use the platform of the World Seniors Snooker Tour to help raise awareness and support the incredible work being undertaken by Alzheimer’s Research UK.“

“Snooker is a sport that brings generations together, and we hope this partnership will allow us to make a meaningful contribution to a cause that deserves all the support it can get.”

The partnership also ties into the charity’s Think Brain Health campaign, which sets out three simple rules to help reduce dementia risk: love your heart, stay sharp and keep connected.

Zoe Dean, Senior Relationship Fundraiser at Alzheimer’s Research UK, said, “We are delighted to be the official charity partner for the World Seniors Snooker Tour. Snooker has such a passionate and engaged community, and this partnership gives us a fantastic opportunity to raise awareness of dementia, inspire people to get involved and raise vital funds for research. Playing snooker is also a great way to stay sharp and keep connected, two key messages of our Think Brain Health campaign that encourages people to take positive steps to look after their brain health.“

Alzheimer’s Society sponsored Talent Campaign of the Year at the 2026 SIAs and is an official partner and category partner again for the 2027 SIAs.

title: Iraq grapples with federation mess and uncertainty over Graham Arnold's future
article_text:
Iraqi football is in disarray. Its federation is consumed by feuds, legal challenges and accusations of political meddling. And now Graham Arnold, the Australian coach who ended the country’s 40-year wait for a World Cup, may be about to take charge of his last match.

Iraqi media report that his successor will be Emad Mohammed, a former national team striker with a patchy record in the dugout.

The Iraqi Football Association is governed by a president chosen by 61 voting delegates drawn from clubs, regional bodies and professional associations. In Iraq, the job brings money, influence and political prestige. So, inevitably, parties and powerful benefactors take an interest in who gets it.

For five years, that man was Adnan Dirjal, a defender from the generation that qualified for the 1986 World Cup and a former sports minister. His deputy was Younis Mahmoud, the revered captain who lifted the 2007 Asian Cup.

The partnership’s collapse played out in public. In 2023, Mahmoud told a television audience that he had tried to curb Dirjal’s authority over contracts relating to the staging of the 2023 Gulf Cup that had been signed without the board’s knowledge. In August 2025, Mahmoud announced that he would stand against him.

World Cup qualification should have made Dirjal untouchable, but Mahmoud prevailed in May by 38 votes to 20, just before the tournament kicked off.

Dirjal stormed out, sarcastically congratulating the politician Mohammed Al Halbousi and Olympic Committee president Aqeel Muftin, both of whom he accused of orchestrating his defeat. Mahmoud’s camp denied any interference, and the Court of Arbitration for Sport has twice refused Dirjal’s requests to suspend the new board pending a final ruling on his challenge to the election.

One of the players who credited Dirjal for his work was Ali Al Hamadi. In an interview with The National, before the World Cup, the striker was asked whether a dressing room which included Kurds, Arabs, Chaldeans and Assyrians, in a country long scarred by division, ever discussed politics.

His response: “I think this is definitely probably the most together it’s ever been. And that’s credit to the staff, that’s credit to Adnan Dirjal as well for his work behind the scenes, recruiting players, the organisation.”

Arnold was Dirjal’s appointment, and the new leadership inherited him weeks before the World Cup. Despite Iraq losing all three of their World Cup matches, Arnold was offered a four-year contract in July but agreed to sign for six months instead, intended to take him through to the 2027 Asian Cup.

He reasoned that a long deal might cost him his passion for the job and leave the federation with an expensive payout. However, the federation's vice-president, Sarmad Abdulilah, subsequently acknowledged that Arnold had also raised serious concerns about administrative failings, including arrangements for training camps, player transport and communications with clubs.

The new leadership began to introduce their own changes. The team’s manager, Mustafa Jalal, was replaced by Dr Mushtaq Kadhim, whose father has long-standing ties to Al Naft, an oil-backed club with a vote in federation elections. Jalal was experienced, fluent in English and was said to have worked well with Arnold’s foreign staff.

On the pitch, Iraq’s results were fuelling criticism. At the Gulf Cup in September, they needed only a draw against an already-qualified Saudi Arabia, but Arnold made changes due to concerns that players already on yellow cards could miss the semi-finals. His side lost 2-0.

But the federation stood by him, publicly reaffirming their confidence in the Australian in October.

Then earlier this month, the Asian Cup was postponed over security threats in Saudi Arabia. Arnold’s contract expires in February, leaving him without the tournament he had stayed on to coach.

Emad is widely tipped to be Arnold’s successor. In July, Mahmoud reportedly told him he would be first choice should talks with Arnold collapse.

On paper, he ticks a few boxes. Born in Kerbala in 1982, he was a striker who won 103 caps and scored 27 goals for Iraq. As a coach, he guided Iraq’s Under-20 side to the final of the 2023 Asian Championship and on to the World Cup in Argentina.

But is he the best candidate? His spells in club football were brief. His Under-23 team exited the 2026 Asian Championship without a victory, after which he said the federation had talked him out of resigning.

In 2024, Fifa banned him for six months over insults aimed at a television presenter, though he denied responsibility for the social media account involved. What makes it all the more interesting is that Emad himself noted in July that Arnold should stay and finish what he started.

At the weekend, Iraqi media reported that Tuesday's match against Iran in Basra would be Arnold's last, regardless of the result. Federation sources claimed the board had agreed he would not continue, although no replacement had been confirmed. Emad is reportedly willing to take over if offered a long-term contract.

Importantly, Mahmoud also recently revealed that the federation was facing a financial crisis with a monthly wage bill of more than 400 million Iraqi dinars for national team coaches and their staff.

But the federation has yet to confirm any decision. Mahmoud said the coach's future would be discussed only when the senior and Olympic teams had finished their current matches, while board member Ghalib Al Zamili insisted the Australian will continue under his current contract.

title: Christian Horner’s private message to Toto Wolff revealed after Kimi Antonelli's 2026 F1 title
article_text:
For Mercedes fans. All the latest from the Silver Arrows, with F1 news, driver updates, car development and race analysis from Brackley and Brixworth.

At the height of their bitter championship battles, the idea of Christian Horner sending Toto Wolff a warm congratulatory text would have seemed entirely fictional to most Formula 1 fans. But following Kimi Antonelli's historic 2026 title victory with Mercedes, the former Red Bull team principal reached out to his old adversary with high praise.

In an exclusive interview with the German publication BILD, Wolff was asked if he had heard from Horner amid the flood of recent congratulations.

Given that Horner was Wolff's fiercest rival for years before his dismissal from Red Bull in July 2025, the interviewer questioned if the Austrian was surprised by the gesture.

"Yes, but that didn't surprise me," Wolff stated. "Christian and I have a respectful relationship. That was already the case back then."

When Wolff made the decision to replace Ferrari-bound Lewis Hamilton with Antonelli, critics actively questioned if the teenager was ready for the immense pressure of a championship-calibre team. Having worked with a similar junior driver pipeline during his time at Red Bull, Horner reached out to commend Wolff for taking that gamble.

When asked to reveal the exact contents of the text message, Wolff shared Horner's private words.

title: Williams unveil special livery for Las Vegas Grand Prix
article_text:
Williams have unveiled a special livery that will adorn their car for the Las Vegas Grand Prix weekend.

The one-off chrome look is a collaboration with the team’s title partner Atlassian, designed to shine under the lights as Alex Albon and Carlos Sainz take to the Las Vegas Strip Circuit. Both drivers will also sport custom race suits and gloves in line with the colour scheme.

In an announcement revealing the livery, Williams stated that the design is “the latest embodiment of Williams and Atlassian’s belief that the fastest way forward is knowing where you have been, which is central to the partnership”.

Team Principal James Vowles commented: “Our next step forward isn’t a matter of reinvention; it’s about evolving from where we’ve been, using the knowledge, context, and information our team shares.

“We’re proud to be working with Atlassian to unlock that near-50-year history and using it as fuel for our future. This spectacular livery reflects that and I’m looking forward to seeing it take to the track under the bright lights of the Vegas Strip.”

Mike Cannon-Brookes, Co-Founder and CEO, Atlassian, added: “The new Williams livery looks great in Las Vegas – but our partnership goes well beyond what you see on the track. We are helping Williams turn their ambition into execution.

“We’re working shoulder to shoulder with the team at Williams to build AI workflows on the Atlassian Teamwork Graph connecting their teams’ expertise, knowledge and projects so they can make smarter, faster decisions.”

title: When is the earliest Antonelli could win the title?
article_text:
POINTS PERMUTATIONS: When could Antonelli win the World Championship?

As Kimi Antonelli continues to lead the standings, F1.com looks at the permutations for when the Mercedes driver could mathematically win the World Championship.

Kimi Antonelli has remained at the top of the drivers’ standings since Round 3 of the campaign in Japan – and his hold on the P1 slot was strengthened following his victory at the United States Grand Prix.

The Italian is now 123 points clear of closest challenger George Russell following the 18th event of the season, while third-placed Lewis Hamilton is now 124 points adrift.

Antonelli has previously insisted that thinking about the title is “exactly what I don’t want to do”, but following his win in Austin, even the Italian started to discuss how close he was to that maiden World Championship crown...

Five rounds remain in the 2026 season, with the next being the Mexico City Grand Prix.

This means that the maximum points score still available is 125, which would be achieved by a driver winning every remaining Grand Prix.

Which drivers are still in contention for the title?

Mathematically, two drivers besides Antonelli are still in contention for the championship – just Russell and Hamilton can beat the Italian now.

However, the realistic likelihood of either taking the title is slim, with their chance of winning based on the possibility of Antonelli failing to score any more points and one of the duo winning every race until the end of the season.

In this scenario, Russell or Hamilton could seal the title in Abu Dhabi.

When could Antonelli claim the World Championship?

Antonelli had a chance of winning the title at the United States Grand Prix, and he almost did it too. He needed to win the race and have Hamilton finish fifth or lower, and Russell finish ninth or lower.

While the 20-year-old held up his end of the bargain with victory in Austin, Hamilton finished fourth and Russell eighth to deny him the title.

But his maximum score means it is very likely that Antonelli will win the title in Mexico City. For this to happen, Antonelli would need to finish at least ninth. If he does so, it does not matter where Russell or Hamilton finish, the title will belong to the Italian.

In other words, Antonelli needs to score just two more points to take the title. If he fails to score, he will still take the title if neither Russell nor Hamilton win the race.

If Antonelli finishes P10, Russell can keep the title fight going to Sao Paulo with a victory.

When can Mercedes clinch the Teams' Championship?

Following their 29-point haul from Austin, Mercedes can seal the Constructors' Championship title in Mexico City, although it remains a long shot with Ferrari still very much in contention.

If they take a 1-2, then the Silver Arrows need Ferrari to score four points or fewer to take the title next weekend.

If Antonelli and Russell take the win and a third place, they need Ferrari to score one point or less.

Any other scenario sees that title battle move on to the next round in Sao Paulo.
